speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how the wound on your right lower leg started and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any changes in the color of your skin around the wound, such as darkening or scaling, and does elevating your leg provide any relief from the swelling? I would also like to assess the wound bed and surrounding tissue for signs of infection or venous stasis changes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that pyelonephritis is a kidney infection and does not cause chronic leg wounds or swelling. Given your history of DVT and chronic edema, this presentation is classic for venous stasis ulcers. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer
